Subject: POC model routing & success criteria — next steps

Thanks again for the demo call earlier — great to learn more about HealthSync's support automation goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an agreed plan for the trial.

Recap of needs you called out:
- Multi-lingual triage for English, Spanish, French (primarily English)
- Fast mean response time target: sub-400ms 95th percentile for single-turn classification/routing requests
- Low-cost fallback for high-concurrency windows
- Privacy: logs retained for 30 days, no PHI stored beyond session in the PoC

Proposed POC scope (2-week technical trial):
1) Inference footprint: streaming classification endpoint + routing logic to two model variants
2) Models to evaluate: primary open model = Llama 2 13B (int8 quantized), fallback = MPT-7B-Instruct (8-bit) — see notes on tokenizer differences below
3) Success metrics: accuracy (routing to correct team) >= 92% on your eval set, latency p95 < 400ms, cost per 1k requests < $X (TBD after baseline run)
4) Ownership:
   - HealthSync: provide labeled eval set (300-500 examples per language), share expected traffic pattern
   - Redwood: spin up the trial cluster, run baseline runs, deliver a dashboard with per-model accuracy/latency/cost
5) Timeline:
   - Thu Apr 16: Data & eval set received from HealthSync
   - Mon Apr 20: Trial environment live, baseline ingestion
   - Fri Apr 24: Results & recommendation, then decision to extend or iterate

Notes about model choice / routing logic:
- Llama 2 13B (quantized) chosen as primary for best instruction-following and multilingual transfer; we’ll enable prefix caching to reduce cold-token cost.
- MPT-7B-Instruct as fallback keeps cost down and is robust for short, structured classification tasks. If we see Spanish/French degradation > 6% compared to English, we'll try Falcon-7B as alternate fallback.
- Routing will be model-level: first query primary, if confidence < threshold or latency spike detected, route to fallback. We can also test a parallel scoring path for quality vs cost trade-off.

Attachments: I attached a short spreadsheet with the proposed success metric breakdown and a network diagram showing the PoC VPC peering requirements.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Anna / Kevin: confirm you can deliver an eval sample (300 per language) by Apr 16 and introduce procurement to start any security paperwork.
- Marissa / Grace: please review the proposed success metrics and pricing guardrails; Marissa can flag any Dedicated capacity considerations.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff once I have confirmation on the dataset.

Cheers,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

- Routing decision: for speed we'll start with a single routing decision (primary vs fallback) per request. If you want label-level routing we can enable that as a follow-up test during an extended trial.

- IP ranges: we will supply a CIDR to whitelist; please expect a single small public IP for the hosted endpoint during the PoC.
